mainTopic: הלל's patience versus שמאי's strictness, and why יראת ה׳ is the treasure that gives תורה its value.
overview: This amud shows how much patience and humility matter, and then how important יראת שמים is. First, a man bets four hundred זוז that he can make הלל angry. He rudely interrupts הלל three times on ערב שבת with insulting questions, but הלל answers each one calmly and never gets upset. Next, a ברייתא tells of three non-Jews who wanted to convert on strange conditions: rejecting תורה שבעל פה, learning the whole תורה on one foot, and becoming כהן גדול. שמאי sends each of them away, but הלל accepts each one and gently guides him to the truth. The three converts later agree that שמאי's impatience nearly drove them away, while הלל's patience brought them under the wings of the שכינה. Then ריש לקיש and רבא explain a פסוק in ישעיה, about the six orders of the משנה and about the six questions a person is asked at judgment. Both conclude that all of this counts only together with יראת ה׳, and רבא shows this with a parable about wheat stored without a preservative. The amud ends as רבה בר רב הונא begins a teaching about a person who has תורה but lacks יראת שמים, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two men make a bet about angering הלל
steps.stepSummary: Two men bet four hundred זוז on whether anyone could make הלל angry, and one of them takes up the challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: They made a bet with each other and said: Whoever goes and makes הלל angry will get four hundred זוז. One of them said: I will make him angry.
steps.whatsHappening: The story begins. Two men bet money on whether someone can get הלל to lose his temper, and one man volunteers to try.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sentence opens mid-thought because the words just before it introduced 'two people' (מעשה בשני בני אדם). The goal of the bet is to provoke הלל until he scolds or snaps. Four hundred זוז is a large sum, which shows how seriously they took the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: They made a bet or wager
A silver coin. Four hundred זוז is a large amount.

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The words 'who wagered with each other' refer to two men who were just introduced earlier.

phrases.english: who made a bet with each other,
phrases.notes: Refers to the two people introduced on the previous amud

phrases.english: they said: whoever will go
and make Hillel angry
will take four hundred zuz.
One of them said:
I will make him angry.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁהִמְרוּ זֶה אֶת זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story introduced on the previous amud, which illustrates the teaching that one should be humble like הלל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bet is set: whoever angers הלל wins four hundred זוז.

steps.title: The man rudely calls הלל on Friday afternoon
steps.stepSummary: On ערב שבת, while הלל is washing his hair, the man shouts rudely outside his house. הלל dresses respectfully, comes out, and kindly invites his question.
steps.simpleTranslation: That day was ערב שבת, and הלל was washing his head. The man went past the door of his house and said: Who here is הלל? Who here is הלל? הלל wrapped himself in a garment and went out to meet him. He said: My son, what do you want? He said: I have a question to ask. הלל said: Ask, my son.
steps.whatsHappening: The man begins his attempt. He chooses a busy, inconvenient moment and calls out disrespectfully, but הלל answers gently. This sets up the first question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The timing is deliberate: ערב שבת is a pressured time, and הלל is in the middle of washing. Shouting 'Who here is הלל?' with no title is disrespectful. Still, הלל stops, dresses with dignity, and calls him 'my son'.

keyTerms.meaning: Friday, the busy time of preparing for שבת
Wrapped himself in a garment, dressing respectfully
My son, a warm way of addressing someone

phrases.english: That day was Shabbat eve,
and Hillel was washing his head.
phrases.notes: He was busy and in the middle of preparing for שבת

phrases.english: He went and passed by the entrance of his house,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: מִי כָּאן הִלֵּל, מִי כָּאן הִלֵּל?
phrases.english: he said: Who here is Hillel, who here is Hillel?
phrases.notes: Said in a rude way, without any title of respect

phrases.english: He wrapped himself and went out to meet him.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: בְּנִי, מָה אַתָּה מְבַקֵּשׁ?
phrases.english: He said to him: My son, what do you want?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: שְׁאֵלָה יֵשׁ לִי לִשְׁאוֹל.
phrases.english: He said to him: I have a question to ask.
He said to him: Ask, my son.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The man begins carrying out the bet from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even when rudely disturbed at a bad time, הלל responds warmly.

steps.title: First insulting question about Babylonians' heads
steps.stepSummary: The man asks why בבליים have oval heads, a jab at הלל, who came from Bavel. הלל praises the question and answers calmly.
steps.simpleTranslation: He asked: Why are the heads of בבליים oval? הלל said: My son, you asked a great question. It is because they do not have skilled midwives.
steps.whatsHappening: The man asks his first silly, insulting question. הלל treats it as a serious question and gives a calm answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הלל was originally from Bavel, so the question is a personal insult in disguise. Instead of getting offended, הלל calls it 'a great question' and explains that the midwives there do not know how to shape a baby's head at birth.

keyTerms.meaning: People from Bavel (Babylonia), where הלל came from

phrases.english: He asked: For what reason
are the heads of Babylonians oval?
phrases.notes: A hidden insult, since הלל was from בבל

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: בְּנִי, שְׁאֵלָה גְּדוֹלָה שָׁאַלְתָּ.
phrases.english: He said to him: My son, you have asked a great question.
Because they do not have skilled midwives.
phrases.notes: The midwives do not shape the newborn's head

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה רָאשֵׁיהֶן שֶׁל בַּבְלִיִּים סְגַלְגַּלּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the question the man said he wanted to ask in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why בבליים have oval heads (really an insult aimed at הלל).

steps.title: Second visit: question about the eyes of Tadmor's people
steps.stepSummary: The man waits an hour, shouts for הלל again, and asks why the people of Tadmor have bleary eyes. הלל again comes out and answers patiently.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and waited an hour, came back and said: Who here is הלל? Who here is הלל? הלל wrapped himself and went out to meet him. He said: My son, what do you want? He said: I have a question. He said: Ask, my son. He asked: Why are the eyes of the people of Tadmor bleary? He said: My son, you asked a great question. It is because they live among the sands.
steps.whatsHappening: The man repeats the exact same rude routine a second time with a new pointless question. הלל responds exactly as kindly as before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The repetition matters: the man waits just long enough for הלל to get back to his washing, then interrupts him again. The question is not urgent at all, yet הלל stops again, dresses again, and explains that sand blows into their eyes.

keyTerms.meaning: People of Tadmor (Palmyra), a desert city

phrases.english: He went and waited one hour,
phrases.notes: A short while, just enough for הלל to return to washing

phrases.aramaic: חָזַר וְאָמַר: מִי כָּאן הִלֵּל, מִי כָּאן הִלֵּל?
phrases.english: he came back and said: Who here is Hillel, who here is Hillel?
He wrapped himself and went out to meet him.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: בְּנִי, מָה אַתָּה מְבַקֵּשׁ?
phrases.english: He said to him: My son, what do you want?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: שְׁאֵלָה יֵשׁ לִי לִשְׁאוֹל.
phrases.english: He said to him: I have a question to ask.
He said to him: Ask, my son.
He asked: For what reason
are the eyes of the people of Tadmor bleary?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: בְּנִי, שְׁאֵלָה גְּדוֹלָה שָׁאַלְתָּ.
phrases.english: He said to him: My son, you have asked a great question.
Because they live among the sands.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָלַךְ וְהִמְתִּין שָׁעָה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the pattern of steps 2 and 3 with a new question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the people of Tadmor have bleary eyes.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because they live among the sands.

steps.title: Third visit: question about Africans' wide feet
steps.stepSummary: A third time, the man waits, shouts, and asks why אפריקיים have wide feet. הלל again answers calmly.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and waited an hour, came back and said: Who here is הלל? Who here is הלל? הלל wrapped himself and went out to meet him. He said: My son, what do you want? He said: I have a question. He said: Ask, my son. He asked: Why do Africans have wide feet? He said: My son, you asked a great question. It is because they live in marshes.
steps.whatsHappening: The same routine happens a third time. הלל still shows no sign of irritation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three times is a full pattern, which shows that הלל's patience is steady and not a one-time act. His answer, that wide feet help people walk through swampy land, is again calm and sensible.

phrases.english: He went and waited one hour,

phrases.aramaic: חָזַר וְאָמַר: מִי כָּאן הִלֵּל, מִי כָּאן הִלֵּל?
phrases.english: he came back and said: Who here is Hillel, who here is Hillel?
He wrapped himself and went out to meet him,

phrases.english: he said to him: My son, what do you want?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: שְׁאֵלָה יֵשׁ לִי לִשְׁאוֹל.
phrases.english: He said to him: I have a question to ask.
He said to him: Ask, my son.
He asked: For what reason
are the feet of Africans wide?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: בְּנִי שְׁאֵלָה גְּדוֹלָה שָׁאַלְתָּ —
phrases.english: He said to him: My son, you have asked a great question —
because they live among the water marshes.
phrases.notes: Wide feet help them walk on swampy ground

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה רַגְלֵיהֶם שֶׁל אַפְרִקִיִּים רְחָבוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third repetition of the same pattern.

steps.title: הלל sits down and invites all his questions
steps.stepSummary: The man says he has many more questions but fears הלל will get angry. הלל dresses, sits down in front of him, and tells him to ask everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I have many questions to ask, and I am afraid you will get angry. הלל wrapped himself and sat before him. He said: All the questions you have to ask, ask.
steps.whatsHappening: The man tries a new tactic and openly hints that הלל might lose patience. הלל responds by sitting down and giving him unlimited time. This sets up the man's final outburst.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, הלל stood at the door. Now he sits down, which shows he is ready to give the man all the time he wants, even on ערב שבת. This removes any chance that he will snap, and it frustrates the man's plan.

keyTerms.meaning: Sat down in front of him

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: שְׁאֵלוֹת הַרְבֵּה יֵשׁ לִי לִשְׁאוֹל,
phrases.english: He said to him: I have many questions to ask,
and I am afraid that you might get angry.
He wrapped himself and sat down before him.
phrases.notes: A sign that he was giving the man his full time

phrases.english: He said to him: All the questions
that you have to ask, ask.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁאֵלוֹת הַרְבֵּה יֵשׁ לִי לִשְׁאוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After three failed attempts, the man changes his approach.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הלל invites unlimited questions instead of becoming impatient.

steps.title: The frustrated man insults הלל and reveals the bet
steps.stepSummary: The man asks if this is the הלל called נשיא ישראל, wishes there would not be many like him, and admits he lost four hundred זוז because of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Are you הלל, whom they call נשיא ישראל? He said: Yes. He said: If it is you, may there not be many like you in Israel. He said: My son, why? He said: Because I lost four hundred זוז because of you.
steps.whatsHappening: Out of frustration, the man insults הלל directly and reveals the bet he lost. הלל still answers calmly and asks him why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the man, not הלל, is the one who has lost his temper. Even after a direct insult, הלל still calls him 'my son' and simply asks for the reason. The man's confession shows the bet has failed.

keyTerms.meaning: The leader (נשיא) of the Jewish people
May there not be many like you

phrases.english: He said to him: Are you Hillel
whom they call 'the Nasi of Israel'?
He said to him: Yes.
He said to him: If it is you,
may there not be many like you in Israel.
He said to him: My son, for what reason?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאִבַּדְתִּי עַל יָדְךָ
phrases.english: He said to him: Because I lost, on account of you,
four hundred zuz.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה הוּא הִלֵּל שֶׁקּוֹרִין אוֹתְךָ נְשִׂיא יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The man gives up on his plan and reveals the bet from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The man admits defeat. He lost the bet because הלל never got angry.

steps.title: הלל's reply: losing the money is worth it
steps.stepSummary: הלל tells the man to watch his own temper, because it is worth losing even eight hundred זוז rather than have הלל lose his patience.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Be careful with your spirit. הלל is worth it that you should lose four hundred זוז, and another four hundred זוז, and הלל will still not get upset.
steps.whatsHappening: הלל ends the story with a gentle lesson: control your temper, and know that הלל will not lose his, no matter the cost to the man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הלל turns the lesson back on the man, who was the one who actually got angry. He says it is worth losing the money again and again rather than for הלל to lose his patience. This proves the opening teaching that one should be humble and patient like הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: Be careful with your spirit, control your temper
Will be upset, will be strict or angry

steps.whatToRemember: הלל stayed patient and respectful through repeated rude interruptions at the worst time, ערב שבת. That is the model of humility and patience this story teaches.
steps.whyThisMatters: This story is the main proof for the teaching that a person should always be humble and patient like הלל and never quick to anger.

phrases.english: He said to him: Be careful with your spirit;
Hillel is worthy

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁתְּאַבֵּד עַל יָדוֹ אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת זוּז
phrases.english: that you should lose on his account four hundred zuz
and another four hundred zuz,
and Hillel will not get upset.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֱוֵי זָהִיר בְּרוּחֲךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: הלל answers the man's complaint from step 7 and closes the story.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: הלל will not lose his temper at any price, so one should be patient and humble like הלל.

steps.title: A non-Jew asks שמאי how many Torahs there are
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא begins a new story. A non-Jew asks שמאי how many Torahs the Jews have, and שמאי answers: two, תורה שבכתב and תורה שבעל פה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: There was a story about a non-Jew who came before שמאי. He said to him: How many Torahs do you have? שמאי said to him: Two, the Written Torah and the Oral Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new story from a ברייתא and sets up the first case. This step lays out the background for the non-Jew's demand in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמאי's answer sets up the main issue of the whole story: the Jewish people have both a written תורה and an oral תורה. The non-Jew's next move will be to accept one and reject the other.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּגוֹי אֶחָד שֶׁבָּא לִפְנֵי שַׁמַּאי.
phrases.english: There was a story about a non-Jew who came before Shammai.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: כַּמָּה תּוֹרוֹת יֵשׁ לָכֶם?
phrases.english: He said to him: How many Torahs do you have?
He said to him: Two,
the Written Torah and the Oral Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּגוֹי אֶחָד שֶׁבָּא לִפְנֵי שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new series of stories that continues the theme of הלל's patience from Steps 1-8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two Torahs: written and oral.

steps.title: The non-Jew rejects the Oral Torah, and שמאי sends him away
steps.stepSummary: The non-Jew says he believes in the תורה שבכתב but not the תורה שבעל פה. He asks to convert on condition that he is taught only the Written Torah. שמאי scolds him and sends him away.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The Written one, I believe you. But the Oral one, I do not believe you. Convert me on condition that you teach me only the Written Torah. שמאי scolded him and sent him out with a rebuke.
steps.whatsHappening: The non-Jew makes his demand to accept only half the תורה, and שמאי refuses him firmly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man wants to convert while rejecting תורה שבעל פה, which is a basic part of Judaism. שמאי treats this as unacceptable and pushes him out. This sets up the contrast with how הלל will handle the same person.

phrases.english: He said to him: The Written one, I believe you,
but the Oral one, I do not believe you.

phrases.aramaic: גַּיְּירֵנִי עַל מְנָת שֶׁתְּלַמְּדֵנִי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב.
phrases.english: Convert me on condition that you teach me only the Written Torah.
He scolded him and sent him out with a rebuke.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁבִּכְתָב אֲנִי מַאֲמִינְךָ, וְשֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה אֵינִי מַאֲמִינְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on שמאי's answer by having the non-Jew accept only one of the two Torahs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמאי refuses a convert who rejects תורה שבעל פה.

steps.title: הלל converts him and teaches the letters, then reverses them
steps.stepSummary: The same man goes to הלל, who converts him. On the first day הלל teaches him the letters א, ב, ג, ד. On the next day הלל switches them around.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before הלל, and הלל converted him. On the first day הלל said to him: א, ב, ג, ד. The next day he reversed the letters for him.
steps.whatsHappening: הלל accepts the man and begins teaching him the alphabet. Then he sets up a test by changing the letters the next day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הלל does not argue with the man directly. He creates a situation that will show the man, from his own experience, that he already depends on a teacher's oral word.
steps.confusionAlert: הלל did not truly accept the condition of 'no Oral Torah.' He converted the man because he was confident that once the man learned, he would come to accept the Oral Torah himself.

phrases.english: He came before Hillel, and he converted him.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹמָא קַמָּא אֲמַר לֵיהּ: א״ב ג״ד.
phrases.english: On the first day he said to him: Alef, bet, gimmel, dalet.
The next day he reversed them for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּא לִפְנֵי הִלֵּל, גַּיְירֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with שמאי's rejection: הלל accepts the same person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הלל accepts the convert and teaches him in a way meant to lead him to the truth.

steps.title: The convert objects that yesterday he was taught differently
steps.stepSummary: The convert complains to הלל: yesterday you did not tell me this.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But yesterday you did not tell me this!
steps.whatsHappening: The convert challenges הלל, because today's lesson contradicts yesterday's lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without noticing, the convert shows that he only knows the letters because הלל told him what they are. His complaint is exactly what הלל wanted him to say.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְהָא אֶתְמוֹל לָא אֲמַרְתְּ לִי הָכִי!
phrases.english: He said to him: But yesterday you did not tell me this!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אֶתְמוֹל לָא אֲמַרְתְּ לִי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to הלל reversing the letters.
steps.kashyaTarget: הלל's reversed teaching of the letters
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Today's teaching contradicts what הלל taught yesterday.

steps.title: הלל: you trusted me for the letters, so trust me for the Oral Torah
steps.stepSummary: הלל answers: weren't you relying on me? Then rely on me for the תורה שבעל פה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Weren't you relying on me? Then rely on me for the Oral Torah too.
steps.whatsHappening: הלל explains the point of his test and ends the first story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even reading the Written Torah depends on a teacher passing down what the letters are. So someone who accepts the Written Torah is already relying on an oral tradition, and he should accept תורה שבעל פה as well.
steps.whatToRemember: The Written Torah cannot be understood without an oral tradition. Even the letters themselves are passed down from teacher to student.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source for the idea that תורה שבכתב depends on תורה שבעל פה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָאו עֲלַי דִּידִי קָא סָמְכַתְּ?
phrases.english: He said to him: Weren't you relying on me?
Then rely on me for the Oral Torah too.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו עֲלַי דִּידִי קָא סָמְכַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the convert's objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the objection itself proves the point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The Written Torah can stand by itself without any oral tradition.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even the Written Torah relies on a teacher's oral word, so the Oral Torah must be accepted too.

steps.title: A second non-Jew wants the whole Torah on one foot
steps.stepSummary: Another non-Jew asks שמאי to convert him on condition that he teaches him the whole תורה while he stands on one foot. שמאי pushes him away with the builder's measuring stick.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another story: a non-Jew came before שמאי and said to him: Convert me on condition that you teach me the entire Torah while I stand on one foot. שמאי pushed him away with the builder's measuring stick that was in his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The second story begins. A non-Jew makes a demand that seems impossible, and שמאי refuses him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The demand sounds like mockery, since the whole תורה cannot be learned that fast. שמאי, a builder by trade, pushes him away with his measuring stick.

phrases.aramaic: שׁוּב מַעֲשֶׂה בְּגוֹי אֶחָד שֶׁבָּא לִפְנֵי שַׁמַּאי.
phrases.english: Another story about a non-Jew who came before Shammai.
He said to him: Convert me on condition
that you teach me the entire Torah
while I am standing on one foot!
He pushed him away with the builder's measuring stick in his hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוּב מַעֲשֶׂה בְּגוֹי אֶחָד שֶׁבָּא לִפְנֵי שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the second of the three stories.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמאי rejects the demand to learn the whole תורה on one foot.

steps.title: הלל: What is hateful to you, do not do to others
steps.stepSummary: הלל converts him and teaches him: what is hateful to you, do not do to your friend. That is the whole תורה, and the rest is explanation. Go and learn.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before הלל, and הלל converted him. He said to him: What is hateful to you, do not do to your friend. That is the entire Torah, and the rest is its explanation. Go and learn it.
steps.whatsHappening: הלל answers the 'one foot' request with one sentence that holds the core of the תורה, and sends the man to study the rest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הלל takes the request seriously instead of treating it as mockery. He gives a single principle, but makes clear that it is only the starting point. The man still has to learn everything else, because the rest explains this principle.
steps.whatToRemember: The one-sentence summary does not replace learning. הלל ends with 'זיל גמור': go and study the rest.

phrases.english: He came before Hillel, and he converted him.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: דַּעֲלָךְ סְנֵי לְחַבְרָךְ לָא תַּעֲבֵיד —
phrases.english: He said to him: What is hateful to you, do not do to your friend —
that is the entire Torah,
and the rest is its explanation; go and learn.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּעֲלָךְ סְנֵי לְחַבְרָךְ לָא תַּעֲבֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows הלל's patient response to the same demand שמאי rejected.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The core of the תורה is not doing to others what is hateful to you; the rest explains it and must be learned.

steps.title: A third non-Jew hears about the כהן גדול's garments and wants to be כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: A non-Jew passing a בית המדרש hears a teacher reading about the priestly garments. He asks who they are for, is told 'for the כהן גדול,' and decides to convert so that he can become כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another story: a non-Jew was passing behind the study hall and heard a teacher reading: 'These are the garments they shall make: a breastplate and an ephod.' He asked: Who are these for? They told him: For the כהן גדול. The non-Jew said to himself: I will go and convert so that they will make me כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: The third story begins. This step sets up the man's motive for converting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier men, this man wants to convert for honor and status. His goal is impossible, because a convert cannot become a כהן. That sets up the lesson to come.

keyTerms.meaning: The breastplate and the apron of the כהן גדול

phrases.english: Another story about a non-Jew
who was passing behind the study hall,
and he heard the voice of a teacher who was saying:
"And these are the garments which they shall make: a breastplate and an ephod."
He said: Who are these for?
They said to him: For the High Priest.
That non-Jew said to himself:
I will go and convert
so that they will make me High Priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוּב מַעֲשֶׂה בְּגוֹי אֶחָד שֶׁהָיָה עוֹבֵר אֲחוֹרֵי בֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the third of the three stories.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The non-Jew wants to convert in order to become כהן גדול.

steps.title: שמאי pushes him away; הלל converts him
steps.stepSummary: The man asks שמאי to convert him on condition that he be made כהן גדול. שמאי pushes him away with the measuring stick. הלל converts him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before שמאי and said to him: Convert me on condition that you make me כהן גדול. שמאי pushed him away with the builder's measuring stick in his hand. He came before הלל, and הלל converted him.
steps.whatsHappening: The same pattern repeats: שמאי rejects the man, and הלל accepts him. This sets up הלל's teaching in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The demand is impossible under הלכה, so שמאי refuses. הלל accepts the man anyway and plans to let him discover the truth through learning.

keyTerms.meaning: That you will make me / appoint me

phrases.english: He came before Shammai,
and said to him: Convert me on condition
that you make me High Priest.
He pushed him away with the builder's measuring stick in his hand.
He came before Hillel, and he converted him.

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּיְּירֵנִי עַל מְנָת שֶׁתְּשִׂימֵנִי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The man acts on the plan he made in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמאי rejects him; הלל accepts him.

steps.title: הלל tells him to first learn the rules of the kingdom
steps.stepSummary: הלל says that only someone who knows the royal protocols is made king, so the man should go learn them. The man goes and studies.
steps.simpleTranslation: הלל said to him: Do they appoint a king unless he knows the rules of the kingdom? Go learn the rules of the kingdom. He went and read the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: הלל does not reject the man's goal. He sends him to study first, which sets up the man's discovery in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הלל compares the כהן גדול to a king: before taking an office, you must know its rules. This sends the man to learn תורה, where he will find the answer by himself.

phrases.english: He said to him: Do they appoint a king
unless he is someone who knows the royal protocols?
Go learn the royal protocols.
He went and read.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלוּם מַעֲמִידִין מֶלֶךְ אֶלָּא מִי שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ טַכְסִיסֵי מַלְכוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: הלל's first words to the man he just converted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One must first learn the rules before taking an office.

steps.title: The convert asks who the verse about the זר is talking about
steps.stepSummary: When the convert reaches the verse 'a זר who comes near shall die,' he asks הלל who it refers to. הלל answers: even דוד, king of ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he reached the verse 'And the outsider who comes near shall be put to death,' he said to הלל: Who is this verse said about? הלל said to him: Even about דוד, king of ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The convert asks a clarifying question about a verse, and הלל answers it. This sets up the convert's own conclusion in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse forbids any non-כהן from doing the Temple service. הלל's answer shows how wide the rule is: even a great king like דוד is counted as a זר.

keyTerms.meaning: The outsider (non-כהן) who comes near shall be put to death

phrases.english: When he reached "And the outsider who comes near shall be put to death,"

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ: מִקְרָא זֶה עַל מִי נֶאֱמַר?
phrases.english: he said to him: About whom is this verse said?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: אֲפִילּוּ עַל דָּוִד מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: He said to him: Even about David, king of Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִקְרָא זֶה עַל מִי נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Result of the study הלל sent him to do.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whom the verse 'the זר who comes near shall die' applies to
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It applies to every non-כהן, even דוד המלך.

steps.title: The convert reasons a קל וחומר and realizes he cannot be כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: The convert reasons by himself: if ישראל, who are called God's beloved children, are still forbidden to serve as a זר, then a convert who came with only his staff and bag is surely forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The convert made a קל וחומר by himself: If ישראל, who are called children of God, and out of His love He called them 'My son, My firstborn, ישראל,' still have it written about them 'the outsider who comes near shall be put to death,' then a simple convert who came with just his staff and his bag, all the more so.
steps.whatsHappening: The convert reaches the conclusion on his own: he can never become כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses a קל וחומר: if the more important group (born Jews, God's 'firstborn') is excluded, then the less established group (a new convert) is surely excluded. הלל never had to tell him no; his learning led him to the truth.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from the lesser to the greater (all the more so)
Israel is My son, My firstborn
With his staff and his traveling bag

steps.whatToRemember: In all three stories, הלל's patience lets the convert come to the truth himself: about the Oral Torah, about the core of the תורה, and about his own place.

phrases.aramaic: נָשָׂא אוֹתוֹ גֵּר קַל וָחוֹמֶר בְּעַצְמוֹ:
phrases.english: That convert reasoned an a fortiori argument by himself:
If Israel, who are called children of God,
and out of the love with which He loved them He called them:
"Israel is My son, My firstborn,"
still it is written about them "And the outsider who comes near shall be put to death" —
a simple convert who came with his staff and his bag,
how much more so.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָשָׂא אוֹתוֹ גֵּר קַל וָחוֹמֶר בְּעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on הלל's answer that even דוד is a זר.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A convert cannot become כהן גדול. The convert understands this himself through a קל וחומר from the verse.

steps.title: The convert tells שמאי he now understands
steps.stepSummary: The convert returns to שמאי and admits he could never be כהן גדול, quoting the פסוק about a זר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before שמאי and said to him: Am I at all fit to be כהן גדול? Isn't it written in the Torah: 'And the outsider who comes near shall be put to death'?
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: the convert goes back to שמאי and admits that he cannot become כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, שמאי pushed him away for asking. Now the convert reaches the same conclusion by himself, through his own learning. His learning changed his request, not a rebuke.

keyTerms.meaning: At all / anything (used here as 'am I at all...?')
An outsider, meaning a non-כהן, in the Temple service

phrases.english: He came before Shammai,
he said to him: Am I at all fit
to be High Priest?
Isn't it written in the Torah:
'And the outsider who comes near shall be put to death'?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּא לִפְנֵי שַׁמַּאי, אָמַר לוֹ: כְּלוּם רָאוּי אֲנִי לִהְיוֹת כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Acts on the realization from step 20 by reporting it to שמאי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The convert himself admits he is unfit to be כהן גדול.

steps.title: The convert blesses הלל for his patience
steps.stepSummary: The convert goes to הלל and blesses him for bringing him close to the שכינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before הלל and said to him: Humble הלל, may blessings rest on your head, for you brought me under the wings of the שכינה.
steps.whatsHappening: The convert now goes to הלל and thanks him warmly for his patience.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With שמאי he only admits his mistake. With הלל he gives a blessing. הלל's patience is what let him reach real faith, even though his original reason for converting was not ideal.

keyTerms.meaning: The wings of the Divine Presence (a phrase for joining the Jewish people)

phrases.english: He came before Hillel,
he said to him: Humble Hillel,
may blessings rest upon your head,
for you brought me close, under the wings of the Divine Presence.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּא לִפְנֵי הִלֵּל, אָמַר לוֹ: עַנְוְותָן הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with the visit to שמאי in step 21
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הלל's patience brought the convert to true closeness to ה׳.

steps.title: The three converts compare שמאי and הלל
steps.stepSummary: All three converts meet and agree: שמאי's strictness almost drove them away, while הלל's patience brought them in.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some time later, the three of them met in one place. They said: שמאי's strictness tried to drive us out of the world. הלל's humility brought us under the wings of the שכינה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the whole series of convert stories with one shared lesson spoken by all three converts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the three converts came with a strange condition. שמאי rejected each one, and הלל accepted each one and guided him. Their joint statement turns the three stories into one clear message about patience.

keyTerms.meaning: Strictness, impatience, being quick to anger

steps.whatToRemember: The three convert stories end with one lesson: הלל's patience brings people close to ה׳, while impatience can push them away forever.
steps.confusionAlert: 'The three' are the three converts from the three separate stories the גמרא told, not three people from this story alone.

phrases.english: Some time later, the three of them met in one place,
they said: The impatience of Shammai
sought to drive us from the world;
the humility of Hillel
brought us close under the wings of the Divine Presence.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְיָמִים נִזְדַּוְּוגוּ שְׁלָשְׁתָּן לִמְקוֹם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the series of convert stories
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Patience like הלל's brings people under the wings of the שכינה. Impatience like שמאי's risks driving them away.

steps.title: ריש לקיש matches a verse to the six orders of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש reads the words of ישעיה לג:ו as hints to the six orders of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: What does the פסוק mean, 'And the faith of your times shall be a strength of salvations, wisdom and knowledge'? 'Faith' is סדר זרעים. 'Your times' is סדר מועד. 'Strength' is סדר נשים. 'Salvations' is סדר נזיקין. 'Wisdom' is סדר קדשים. 'And knowledge' is סדר טהרות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. ריש לקיש explains a פסוק by matching each of six words to one of the six orders of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The six words of the פסוק line up in order with זרעים, מועד, נשים, נזיקין, קדשים, and טהרות. This sets up the next line, where the same פסוק adds something beyond all six orders.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written (a formula for explaining a פסוק)
An order, one of the six sections of the משנה

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
'And the faith of your times shall be
a strength of salvations, wisdom and knowledge, etc.'?
'Faith' — this is the Order of Seeds.
'Your times' — this is the Order of Festivals.
'Strength' — this is the Order of Women.
'Salvations' — this is the Order of Damages.
'Wisdom' — this is the Order of Holy Things.
'And knowledge' — this is the Order of Purities.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: מַאי דִכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New aggadic topic about the conduct of חכמים and the value of Torah
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The six words of the פסוק hint to the six orders of the משנה.

steps.title: Even so, fear of ה׳ is the treasure
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש finishes: even after all six orders, 'יראת ה׳ is his treasure.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And even so: 'The fear of ה׳ is his treasure.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש reads the end of the same פסוק to teach that fear of Heaven is above all the learning he just listed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All of the משנה is called valuable, but the פסוק ends by calling יראת ה׳ the 'treasure.' That makes fear of Heaven the storehouse that holds and protects all the learning.

keyTerms.meaning: Fear of ה׳, fear of Heaven

phrases.english: And even so,
'the fear of the Lord is his treasure.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכִי, יִרְאַת ה׳ הִיא אוֹצָרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes ריש לקיש's reading of the פסוק
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Mastery of all six orders of the משנה is still second to יראת שמים.

steps.title: רבא: the questions asked at the heavenly judgment
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads the same פסוק as six questions a person is asked when he comes before the heavenly court.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: When a person is brought to judgment, they ask him: Did you do business honestly? Did you set times for Torah? Did you work at having children? Did you wait hopefully for the redemption? Did you dig deeply into wisdom? Did you understand one thing from another?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second reading of the same פסוק. He turns each word into a question asked in the heavenly judgment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש read the words as areas of learning. רבא reads them as areas of living. 'Faith' becomes honest business, 'times' becomes fixed Torah study, 'strength' becomes having children, and so on.

keyTerms.meaning: Did you do business (literally: carry and give)
Did you hope for the redemption

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the famous list of six questions at judgment. It shows that honesty in business is the very first question.

phrases.english: Rava said:
At the time that they bring a person in for judgment,
they say to him:
Did you conduct business faithfully?
Did you set fixed times for Torah?
Did you engage in having children?
Did you await salvation?
Did you delve deeply into wisdom?
Did you understand one matter from another?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁמַּכְנִיסִין אָדָם לְדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second reading of the same פסוק used by ריש לקיש
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The words of the פסוק are six questions asked at the heavenly judgment.

steps.title: Without fear of ה׳, none of it counts
steps.stepSummary: רבא concludes: even after all six, if יראת ה׳ is his treasure, then yes; if not, then no.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even so: if the fear of ה׳ is his treasure, yes. If not, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his reading with the end of the פסוק. Fear of Heaven decides whether all the rest is worth anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא goes a step further than ריש לקיש. ריש לקיש called יראת ה׳ the greatest. רבא says that without it, the other achievements have no value at all.

phrases.english: And even so,

phrases.aramaic: אִי יִרְאַת ה׳ הִיא אוֹצָרוֹ — אִין,
phrases.english: if the fear of the Lord is his treasure — yes,
if not — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכִי, אִי יִרְאַת ה׳ הִיא אוֹצָרוֹ — אִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's list with the deciding factor
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All good deeds and learning count only if יראת שמים is present.

steps.title: Parable of wheat stored without a preservative
steps.stepSummary: A man tells his agent to store wheat. When he hears no חומטון was mixed in, he says it would have been better not to bring it up at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like a man who told his agent: Bring up a כור of wheat to the attic for me. The agent went and brought it up. The man asked: Did you mix in a קב of חומטון for me? He said: No. The man said: It would have been better if you had not brought it up at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא illustrates his point with a parable. Wheat without a preservative rots, just as Torah without fear of Heaven spoils.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חומטון is a small amount, but it keeps the whole pile from rotting. In the same way, יראת שמים protects all of a person's Torah. Without it, the whole effort goes to waste.

keyTerms.meaning: A substance (possibly sand) mixed in to keep worms out of grain

phrases.english: A parable: a person who said to his agent:
Bring up a kor of wheat to the attic for me.
He went and brought it up for him.
He said to him: Did you mix into it for me
a kav of preservative?
He said to him: No.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: מוּטָב אִם לֹא הֶעֱלֵיתָה.
phrases.english: He said to him: It would have been better had you not brought it up.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָשָׁל לְאָדָם שֶׁאָמַר לִשְׁלוּחוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates רבא's conclusion with a parable
steps.raayaObject: Without יראת שמים, תורה and מצוות lose their value
steps.raayaSupportSource: The parable of wheat stored without חומטון, which rots

steps.title: A seller may mix preservative into grain
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל teaches that a seller may mix a קב of חומטון into a כור of grain without worrying that it is cheating.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל: A person may mix a קב of חומטון into a כור of grain, and he does not need to worry.
steps.whatsHappening: Connected to the parable, the גמרא brings a halachic teaching about mixing חומטון into grain that is being sold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think that selling חומטון at the price of wheat is a kind of theft. The ברייתא says it is allowed, because the preservative is needed to keep the grain good. This matches the parable: the חומטון is a necessary part of stored grain.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל

steps.confusionAlert: 'He need not worry' is about a seller worrying about theft or cheating. It is not about anything to do with the wheat itself.

phrases.english: It was taught in the school of Rabbi Yishmael:
A person may mix a kav of preservative
into a kor of grain,
and he need not be concerned.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: מְעָרֵב אָדָם קַב חוֹמְטוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A halachic side note tied to the חומטון in the parable
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A seller may mix a קב of חומטון into a כור of grain without it counting as cheating.

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא introduces a person who has תורה but lacks something
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא opens a new statement about a person who has תורה in him but is missing something important.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: Any person who has Torah in him, but does not have...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבה בר רב הונא, and this passage is only its opening words. It is setting up a comparison that finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far רבה בר רב הונא only describes the person: he has תורה, but something is missing. Based on the previous steps (ריש לקיש and רבא on יראת ה׳ as the real treasure), we can expect the missing thing to be יראת שמים. The full point, including the comparison, comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Any person, introducing a general rule
He has Torah in him, meaning he has learned and knows Torah
But he does not have... (the missing quality is named on the next amud)

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is unfinished here. Do not try to work out the whole teaching yet. The missing quality and the comparison come on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
Any person who has Torah in him
but does not have
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ תּוֹרָה וְאֵין בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme from ריש לקיש and רבא that תורה must come with יראת ה׳. This is a new אמורא adding his own teaching on the same idea.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: (Opening only) A person who has תורה but lacks a key quality. The rest of the statement comes on the next amud.
